launch.note: $DEFICIT was created on mainnet on 2026-10-13 through the Burnticker LaunchLab platform. Its rules were locked on chain first (rules sha256 8e3e8b66…), then the coin was created, then 3 SOL was seeded into its burn pool as a disclosed gift. The keeper signed the baseline reading the same evening.

rehearsal.note: The devnet rehearsal coin ran at 1% per $1B (the mainnet rule is 2%); its two executed burns are real devnet transactions anyone can check.

firstBurnPath.line: Nothing burns until the curve fills and the debt rises. $DEFICIT first has to graduate at 85 SOL raised, and its pool has to be registered and verified. Only then can a Treasury reading with at least one full $1B unit start a burn.

demo.summary: Treasury's Debt to the Penny rose $23.92B from 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-06, which is 23 units. The rule asked for 0.104 SOL of the 0.506 SOL burn pool. At the time the program still limited how much one crank could spend, so 0.0201 SOL bought 4,010,874.87 $DEFICIT. Every token bought was burned in the same transaction, and the rest carried over to the next crank. That limit is gone now: one crank spends the rule's full share in one run.

phase.label: soft launch ($DEFICIT created on mainnet)
phase.line: Burnticker is in soft launch. Both programs were deployed on mainnet on 2026-10-11 and upgraded to round 4 (end sinks and pairs) on 2026-10-12 through the Squads vault, which holds the upgrade authority. On 2026-10-15 the burn program (burn_receipts) was upgraded again, to round 5 (a coin may burn another coin's token, a finished rule's leftover may be burned as SOL, and a carried spend can be bought without a new reading), through the same vault; the pair program (pair_curve) stays on round 4. On 2026-10-21 the burn program was upgraded through the vault once more, still round 5, so that it registers a coin's trading pool on the fee tier LaunchLab actually used. $DEFICIT, the operator's first coin, was created on mainnet on 2026-10-13 and is on its curve; its keeper signs each Treasury reading. Creator launches opened the same evening, and the first coin made through the site, $PHINFLWIN, was created that night by the operator's own wallet. $REHEARSAL is a test coin the operator made on Oct 11 to check fees and signing. It is kept off the coin list and shown on the Test coins page, linked from the Trust page, so you can see it exists, not so you trade it. On 2026-10-25 both programs were upgraded again through the vault: the burn program (burn_receipts), still round 5, no longer limits what one burn spends, so a burn spends the rule's full share of its pool in one run, and the pair program (pair_curve), still round 4, was rebuilt against it.

mainnet.why: The owner decided on 2026-10-11, and again on 2026-10-12, to keep the mainnet vault's time lock at 0, so that deploy and config fixes are not delayed. While it is 0, a 2-of-3 vote can act at once.
mainnet.keyControl: The vault has three keys but only two controllers. The owner holds members A and B, which are two of the three keys, so the owner alone meets the 2-of-3 threshold. Member C is a person outside the operator who holds the third key and is not named publicly. While the owner holds two keys, the third key adds no independent approval.

releaseRequirements.text: Deploy both programs on mainnet with the Squads vault as upgrade authority. This was done on 2026-10-11; the record is docs/burnkeeper/evidence/mainnet-deploy-2026-10-11/deploy.json.
Make the first real burn on mainnet with $REHEARSAL.
Add an independent second signer. Creator launches opened on 2026-10-13 without one, so until it is added one operator key signs every reading.
Build the end-of-rule sink (program round 4). It is built and deployed on mainnet and devnet, with a devnet run on record.

Upgrade the burn program to round 5 on mainnet through the Squads vault. This was done on 2026-10-15 (vault transaction 3); the read-back is docs/burnkeeper/evidence/mainnet-round5/onchain-verify-after.log.
Raise the mainnet Squads time lock from 0 to 48 h. The owner's decision is to do this at least a week after the soft launch.
Set up the TheSportsDB license key for sports settlement. This was done on 2026-10-11, and the key is set on the mainnet host.
Reproduce the verified build in solana-verify's Docker image.
Sign the operator's statement with the developer fee wallet.
Compile the mainnet operator treasury and LaunchLab platform into both programs.

design: Rules are locked at launch; a different rule is a different coin.

In a pair, the winner takes the burn. Fees from both coins burn the winner's supply. The round 4 program carries this on devnet and mainnet; the host flag for pair launches is on, and creator launches have been open since the evening of 2026-10-13.

When a rule ends and resolves, its leftover burn pool goes to a sink, which is the contest's winner or else $DEFICIT. The round 4 program brought this to devnet and mainnet, and round 5 keeps it; it has run on devnet (the devnet round 4 evidence folder), and no mainnet rule has ended yet.

There is no burn-pool cap and no limit on how much one burn spends: by owner decision on 2026-10-25 both burn caps were removed from the program, so one crank spends the rule's full share in one run, and the platform authority no longer holds a cap-raise power. A carried spend (a spend under the floor, or one that met a pool that could not trade) is bought in one piece without a new reading, by crank_carried. After a rule ends, the carried spend is still bought on the coin: for 30 days after a resolved end the end paths leave it in place, and only after that do they move it on.
The Squads 2-of-3 vault holds the upgrade authority. As the last step it is to be set to none, which is not done yet.
